title: Supporting his family and keeping up his chops
summary: He supported parents and sisters and kept playing big bands.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Day jobs: musicians working outside music

blocks.x: Well, I had about, I figure, 30 good years, I made a great deal of money and I needed a great deal of money because, well, you know, with two children to put through school, I supported my mother and father, two sisters and three nieces because one of my sisters was deserted by her husband. So what with one thing and another, you needed all you could earn. Living in New York is not the cheapest place

in the world. That's primarily why I went in that field. Throughout all the years I would still try to get a night time job in a club with some big band, you know, or I would even take off, go out of town for three or four weeks, just to play with a band.
That's what you call keeping up. Which some of the other guys didn't do.

Well, no, most of them didn't. In fact, I got a lot of criticism, friendly ridicule about it. I have a couple of friends, very good trumpet players, one of them says, 'I don't take my trumpet out of the case unless I get paid for it.' But that kind of attitude for me would have been very dangerous. I had to keep practicing all the time.
